pr_title: upgrades: repair broken 22.1 migration so 22.2 migration works
pr_body:
This also fixes the logic which allowed the 22.1 migration to proceed in the
first place. This will need to be backported to 22.2. Any users which upgraded
from 21.2->22.1->22.2.did_not_contain_this_patch will not have the correct
indexes on their system.statement_diagnostics_requests table.

Fixes https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/91300

Release note (bug fix): Fixed a bug which caused a migration in 22.1 to fail
to drop an index on system.statement_diagnostics_requests and, in turn, caused
upgrades from 22.1->22.2 which had used the previous, faulty upgrade migration
to now fail to create a new index with the same name as the index which had
been thought to have been dropped.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/91304)
First two commits are https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/91296. I haven't tested this, so it's a draft while CI runs.

issue_context.title: upgrades: migration from 21.2 to 22.2 will fail to create correct index on statement diagnostics
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

In 22.1 we attempted to drop an index on `system.statement_diagnostics_requests` called `completed_idx` and replace it with `completed_idx_v2`. Sadly the migration in 22.1 to do this didn't quite work. I think it didn't work because it didn't specify the table and the internal executor must not have been in the right database. The trick to use `IF NOT EXISTS` blinded us to that fact. See here

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/6fdb8f55c6e3224d1d4b8bb2b5f7e757d57d29df/pkg/migration/migrations/alter_statement_diagnostics_requests.go#L36

The bug really manifests itself in 22.2, when we try to now remove `completed_idx_v2` and replace it with a new version, but call it `completed_idx`. In the common case, we just straight-up skip this migration because we ignore the set of stored columns when deciding whether we've already done a migration here: 
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/d860e152bcb3f4bcb4286af5018581ebd48f87c7/pkg/upgrade/upgrades/schema_changes.go#L245-L248

This bug evolved over two changes, but the most recent culprit is https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/72491 which removed this check to make their migration seem to work. I'm not sure why this change was made, but it was definitely wrong.

The pickle in all of this is that if you go from 21.2 or earlier to 22.2 you'll not have the right index for the fancy new statement diagnostics stuff. It'll be painful to fix this after the fact. 

**To Reproduce**

```
roachprod stage local release v21.2.17
roachprod start local
roachprod stop local
roachprod stage local release v22.1.9
roachprod start local
roachprod sql local -- -e 'set cluster setting version = crdb_internal.node_executable_version(); show create table system.statement_diagnostics_requests'
```

You'll find:

```
                   table_name                  |                                                    create_statement
-----------------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  system.public.statement_diagnostics_requests | CREATE TABLE public.statement_diagnostics_requests (
                                               |     id INT8 NOT NULL DEFAULT unique_rowid(),
                                               |     completed BOOL NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
                                               |     statement_fingerprint STRING NOT NULL,
                                               |     statement_diagnostics_id INT8 NULL,
                                               |     requested_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
                                               |     min_execution_latency INTERVAL NULL,
                                               |     expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL,
                                               |     CONSTRAINT "primary" PRIMARY KEY (id ASC),
                                               |     INDEX completed_idx (completed ASC, id ASC) STORING (statement_fingerprint),
                                               |     INDEX completed_idx_v2 (completed ASC, id ASC) STORING (statement_fingerprint, min_execution_latency, expires_at),
                                               |     FAMILY "primary" (id, completed, statement_fingerprint, statement_diagnostics_id, requested_at),
                                               |     FAMILY fam_6_min_execution_latency (min_execution_latency),
                                               |     FAMILY fam_7_expires_at (expires_at)
                                               | )
(1 row)

```

Notice the index we had hoped to drop.

**Additional context**
@Xiang-Gu had not yet written https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/77970 which would have caught this bug. 

Uncovered when trying to remove this bug here: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/91296

Jira issue: CRDB-21195
comments: The fix here is to augment the migration to drop the old index correctly ahead of time so the new index always succeeds and to do the proper check. It's not hard, but if we don't backport it to the GA release, we're going to have a bad time.

review_comments:
Alternatively, this might also defeat the linter:
```
idx, _ := existing.FindIndexWithName("completed_idx")
if idx == nil {
  return true, nil
}
```
